articles.title: The Bug Lives at the Seam, Not in the Logic
articles.excerpt: The encrypted secret was bytes. It round-tripped perfectly in the in-memory store. The unit tests passed. In Postgres, the column was JSON, and bytes is not JSON-serializable. The secret store blew up…
articles.body: The encrypted secret was bytes . It round-tripped perfectly in the in-memory store. The unit tests passed. In Postgres, the column was JSON, and bytes is not JSON-serializable. The secret store blew up at the one boundary the in-memory test never crossed. That was the pattern of the entire v0.2.0 field test on HivePlane . The hard part wasn't the logic — it was the data model and the boundaries. Every defect was a value that was fine in Python and broke one step later, at a persistence seam. This is the article about tracing each value across every persistence boundary — because the bug lives one boundary further than your unit test.
articles.author: Debashish Ghosal

articles.title: SnapInvoice: My AI-Powered Receipt Sorter for Freelancers
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle I built SnapInvoice, a lightweight, mobile-first web app designed for freelancers, independent contractors, and…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built I built SnapInvoice, a lightweight, mobile-first web app designed for freelancers, independent contractors, and small business owners. Every tax season, freelancers waste hours manually sorting through stacks of paper receipts, fuel bills, and vendor invoices to log them into spreadsheets. SnapInvoice solves this by allowing users to instantly snap a photo of any receipt using their mobile phone camera, parsing out the merchant name, date, amount, and tax category automatically. Freelancers and micro-entrepreneurs who hate tedious bookkeeping would gladly pay a small subscription fee to save hours of manual data entry every month.

articles.title: My import worked on clean data. Messy data broke it six ways.
articles.excerpt: The first version of our Harvest import worked great. On my test account. Which had three clients, two projects, and nothing weird in it at all. Some context. I'm building Sheaf, a time tracking and i…
articles.body: The first version of our Harvest import worked great. On my test account. Which had three clients, two projects, and nothing weird in it at all. Some context. I'm building Sheaf , a time tracking and invoicing app for small agencies. A lot of the people trying it are leaving Harvest after its price change, and the first thing they ask is whether they can bring their history with them. So the import matters more than almost anything else in the app. If it gets someone's invoices wrong, they're gone. Real accounts aren't three clients and two projects. They're years of stuff. Old clients, deleted projects, invoices in four currencies, notes someone pasted a whole email into. So before letting anyone near it, I made a fake account that looked like it had been used for years.

articles.title: Debugging an Aged Domain Before You Buy It: A Wayback Status-Code Walkthrough
articles.excerpt: By Lucy Kim, co-founder of Karma.Domains Developers who buy an old domain for a side project usually check one number, see a decent authority score, and click buy. I treat it like a service I'm inheri…
articles.body: By Lucy Kim, co-founder of Karma.Domains Developers who buy an old domain for a side project usually check one number, see a decent authority score, and click buy. I treat it like a service I'm inheriting from someone else and read its logs first. For a domain, the logs are the Wayback Machine archive. Why bother with an old domain at all An aged domain is one that has been online for years and is now available to register or buy. Search engines already know it, it may carry backlinks built over a long time, and sometimes a bit of direct or referral traffic still arrives. The risk is the part nobody puts in the listing: the previous owner could have run a doorway or a link network on it, and age won't undo that.

articles.title: How to Build Reliable Work Handoffs Between AI Agents in TypeScript
articles.excerpt: Making AI Agent Workflows More Reliable with Work Orders, Work Reports, and MCP AI agents can generate code, research problems, and execute tasks. But what happens when one agent finishes its work and…
articles.body: Making AI Agent Workflows More Reliable with Work Orders, Work Reports, and MCP AI agents can generate code, research problems, and execute tasks. But what happens when one agent finishes its work and another needs to continue? The challenge isn't just passing a message. It's preserving the task requirements, decisions, results, and remaining work in a form that another agent can understand and validate. I've been building two npm packages to explore a more structured approach to this problem. The problem with unstructured agent handoffs Imagine a research agent that investigates a problem and passes its findings to a coding agent. A simple message might contain the result, but it may leave important questions unanswered: What exactly was the agent asked to do?

articles.title: GBase Database Installation Troubleshooting: 5 Common Causes and Fixes
articles.excerpt: When a GBase Database (GBase 8s) installation fails, don't assume the installation command is the problem. Missing dependencies, insufficient disk space, port conflicts, and incorrect permissions are…
articles.body: When a GBase Database (GBase 8s) installation fails, don't assume the installation command is the problem. Missing dependencies, insufficient disk space, port conflicts, and incorrect permissions are often better places to start. Here are five practical checks to help troubleshoot GBase Database installation and startup issues systematically. 1. Missing System Dependencies Typical error: error while loading shared libraries: libaio.so.1: cannot open shared object file How to check: On RPM-based Linux systems, verify whether the required package is installed: rpm -q libaio If it is missing, confirm that it is required for your GBase 8s version and operating system before installing it: sudo yum install libaio Other libraries may also be required, depending on the platform.

articles.title: iPhone Duo is here - and it's not one screenshot size, it's two
articles.excerpt: iPhone Duo ships with two displays that share an aspect ratio but not a pixel size: the outer screen is 1398 x 2034 and the inner one 2007 x 2853. App Store Connect treats them as two separate device…
articles.body: iPhone Duo ships with two displays that share an aspect ratio but not a pixel size: the outer screen is 1398 x 2034 and the inner one 2007 x 2853. App Store Connect treats them as two separate device classes - supplying one does not cover the other. So if your app runs on Duo, "a set of screenshots" quietly became "two sets of screenshots". Here's what actually changes, and how to produce both sets without redoing your layouts twice. What a foldable changes The ratio is the same, so your content scales proportionally. The pixel dimensions are not, and neither is the placement: folded and unfolded screenshots go to their own slots in App Store Connect. The practical consequence is layout, not just size.
articles.author: Clican

articles.title: Claude Code Agent Loop Deep Dive (6): From SSE Events to Character-by-Character Rendering
articles.excerpt: In the earlier articles, calling an LLM looked like one atomic operation: response = call_llm(messages) In reality, it is not atomic at all. The Anthropic API streams its response through Server-Sent…
articles.body: In the earlier articles, calling an LLM looked like one atomic operation: response = call_llm ( messages ) In reality, it is not atomic at all. The Anthropic API streams its response through Server-Sent Events (SSE) . While the model generates, it sends fragments to the client. The text that appears character by character in Claude Code is not displayed after a complete paragraph is ready—it is rendered as those fragments arrive. This article follows that stream from the API to the UI: the six event types, how fragments become a complete assistant message, how partial tool JSON is handled, and why the interface can keep accepting user intent while a query is running.

articles.title: Rep. Ritchie Torres Introduces Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Digital Games
articles.excerpt: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than having a license.
articles.body: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than merely buying a license that gives you permission to play them. The bill, known as The Power to the Players Act, would direct the Fedral Trade Commission (FTC) to establish regulations that would protect gamers and their digital libraries. In short, Torres wants to ensure that when you buy a digital game, you actually own it, as opposed to getting a license that can be revoked. Additionally, the bill would require online games to have offline functionality, so that when servers are shut down, the content can still be played by those who own the game.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.

articles.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long his…
articles.body: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars’ orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 . articles.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for the US Space Force (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15), on the 114th Falcon 9 mission of the year.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15). A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today at 8:01 p.m. EDT (5:01 p.m. local time; 0001 GMT on Oct. 16), rising into clear blue skies above the Golden State's central coast. Such visibly striking launches are far from guaranteed; Vandenberg and its scenic surroundings are often blanketed by fog, making rocket watching in the area a dicey proposition. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship shortly after launching the USSF-481 mission on Oct. 15, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) This evening's launch kicked off the USSF-481 mission, which is delivering mysterious payloads to an undisclosed location in the final frontier.
